queries.ground_truth_answer: The DPO must be consulted when carrying out a DPIA; the views of the DPO must be documented; the DPO's advice should include what information needs to be gathered and how the DPIA should be structured.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the adequacy of a third country's data protection?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The Commission assesses the rule of law, respect for human rights, relevant legislation, existence of independent supervisory authority, international commitments, and third country membership of international agreements.

queries.query: What conditions apply to sub-processing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The processor shall not engage sub-processors without prior specific or general written authorisation of the controller; sub-processors are bound by the same obligations; the processor remains liable to the controller.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the obligation to implement data protection by default?
queries.ground_truth_answer: By default, only personal data necessary for each specific purpose should be processed; settings must be privacy-friendly; data subjects must not have to take action to reduce processing.

queries.query: What conditions apply for supervisory authorities to carry out joint operations?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Supervisory authorities may conduct joint investigations; the supervisory authority of the country where the operation takes place remains responsible; costs are shared on agreed terms.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the liability of the controller and processor for damages?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Any controller involved in the processing is liable for damage caused by non-compliant processing; the processor is liable if it has not complied with GDPR or controller's instructions; they may be exempted if not responsible for the event.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right of rectification?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The data subject has the right to have inaccurate personal data corrected without undue delay; if the data is incomplete, the right extends to having it completed considering the purpose.

queries.query: What conditions apply to restricting the obligation to provide information?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The obligation to provide information to data subjects may be restricted by legislative measures when necessary for national security, public security, defence, or other specified public interests.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the power of supervisory authority to publish a report?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Each supervisory authority shall draw up an annual report on its activities and publish it; the report shall be transmitted to the national parliament, government, and other designated authorities.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right to object to profiling?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The data subject may object to profiling where it is for direct marketing; for other processing the data subject must show grounds relating to their situation; if the profiling leads to automated decision-making Article 22 also applies.

queries.query: What conditions apply to processing of data for social protection purposes?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Processing of special category data may be carried out for reasons of substantial public interest in social protection; Member State law must provide appropriate and specific measures to safeguard the data subject.

queries.query: What conditions apply to international transfers under emergency measures?
queries.ground_truth_answer: In exceptional circumstances a supervisory authority may adopt provisional measures with immediate effect; the measures shall not last more than three months; the Board must be immediately informed.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right of data subjects to obtain information about logic in automated decisions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The data subject has the right to obtain meaningful information about the logic involved, the significance and envisaged consequences of such processing; this right applies to all automated decision-making.

queries.query: What conditions apply when processing is necessary for the performance of a task in the public interest?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The task must be laid down by Union or Member State law; the basis must not require consent; the scope of the task must be specified; the basis must be proportionate to the objective.

queries.query: What conditions apply to accreditation of certification bodies?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Certification bodies must be accredited by the national accreditation body or by the supervisory authority; they must demonstrate independence and expertise in data protection.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the principle of accountability?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The controller must be able to demonstrate compliance with GDPR principles; documentation of processing activities, privacy impact assessments, DPO appointment, and policy records all contribute to accountability.

queries.query: What conditions apply to emergency access for vital interests?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Processing for vital interests is only available as a last resort; for special categories it requires that the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; the exception cannot be used as a regular basis.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right to portability when data is inferred or derived?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Portability does not cover inferred data or data created by the controller; it only covers data provided by the data subject or observed from their activity; derived or inferred data is excluded.

queries.query: What conditions must be met for a data subject to invoke the right to restriction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Restriction must be lifted before re-processing; the data subject must be informed before the restriction is lifted; data under restriction may only be processed for establishment of legal claims or with the data subject's consent.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right of access in the employment context?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The right of access exists in the employment context; employers may restrict access under Member State law to protect the interests of the employer only where strictly necessary.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the supervisory authority's power to authorise transfers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The supervisory authority may authorise contractual clauses based on assessment of appropriate safeguards; such authorisations must be reviewed periodically; the Commission may decide they apply Union-wide.

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right to be forgotten in relation to search engines?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The controller who made the data public must take reasonable steps to inform processors including search engines to erase links; the right must be balanced against freedom of expression and information.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 24 together define the accountability framework?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5 sets out the data protection principles including accountability; Article 24 requires the controller to implement measures to demonstrate compliance; together they require both substantive compliance and the ability to prove it.

queries.query: How do Articles 13 and 14 together create a comprehensive transparency regime?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 13 applies when data is collected directly from the data subject; Article 14 applies when it is not; together they ensure data subjects always receive information regardless of how their data was obtained.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 7 interact for consent-based processing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6(1)(a) makes consent a lawful basis; Article 7 sets out the conditions for valid consent; together they define both the legal basis and the conditions that must be met for that basis to be valid.

queries.query: How do Articles 35 and 36 together protect against high-risk processing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 35 requires a DPIA before processing that is likely to result in high risk; Article 36 requires prior consultation with the supervisory authority if the DPIA shows high residual risk; they create a graduated risk management framework.

queries.query: How do Articles 28 and 32 together govern processor security obligations?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 28 requires controllers to use only processors providing sufficient guarantees; Article 32 requires both controllers and processors to implement appropriate security measures; the processor agreement must include the security obligation.

queries.query: How do Articles 33 and 34 create a two-level breach notification system?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 33 requires notification to the supervisory authority within 72 hours; Article 34 requires notification to data subjects when there is high risk; together they ensure both regulators and affected individuals are informed.

queries.query: How do Articles 44 and 49 relate for international transfers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 44 establishes the general principle that transfers must comply with Chapter V; Article 49 provides derogations for exceptional situations where no adequacy decision or safeguards exist; Article 49 is a last resort exception to the general rule in Article 44.

queries.query: How do Articles 83 and 58 work together to enforce GDPR?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 58 gives supervisory authorities their enforcement powers including the power to impose fines; Article 83 specifies the maximum fines and the criteria for setting them; Article 58 is the power and Article 83 is the limit.

queries.query: How do Articles 26 and 28 compare in controllers and processors?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 26 governs joint controllers who together determine purposes and means; Article 28 governs processors who process on behalf of a controller; joint controllers share accountability while a processor is subordinate to the controller.

queries.query: How do Articles 17 and 19 work together in the right to erasure?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 17 gives the right to erasure; Article 19 requires the controller to notify recipients of the erasure; together they ensure the data subject's erasure request reaches all parties who received the data.

queries.query: How do Articles 55 and 56 determine which supervisory authority has jurisdiction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 55 gives each supervisory authority competence for its own Member State; Article 56 designates the lead supervisory authority for cross-border processing; the lead authority is the main interlocutor for cross-border cases.

queries.query: How do Articles 60 and 65 together resolve disagreements between supervisory authorities?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 60 provides for cooperation between the lead and concerned supervisory authorities; Article 65 provides for binding decisions by the Board when consensus cannot be reached; the Board resolves deadlocks.

queries.query: How do Articles 22 and 4 define automated decision-making?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 4 defines profiling as automated processing to evaluate aspects of a natural person; Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions producing significant effects; together they define both the concept and its legal limits.

queries.query: How do Articles 40 and 42 provide alternative compliance mechanisms?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 40 provides for codes of conduct as a soft compliance tool; Article 42 provides for certification as a formal compliance demonstration; codes apply to sectors while certification applies to individual controllers and processors.

queries.query: How do Articles 77 and 79 give data subjects different routes to remedy?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 77 gives data subjects the right to complain to a supervisory authority; Article 79 gives the right to judicial remedy against a controller; both routes may be pursued simultaneously and are complementary.

queries.query: How do Articles 78 and 79 complement each other in judicial remedies?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 78 provides for judicial remedy against supervisory authority decisions; Article 79 provides for judicial remedy against controllers and processors; together they ensure that data subjects have court access against all parties.

queries.query: How do Articles 46 and 47 differ as transfer mechanisms?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 46 provides a range of appropriate safeguards for transfers; Article 47 specifically deals with binding corporate rules which are one of those safeguards; BCRs require approval from a supervisory authority while standard contractual clauses do not.

queries.query: How do Articles 82 and 83 together define liability and administrative penalties?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 82 provides for civil liability and compensation for damage caused by non-compliance; Article 83 provides for administrative fines; they are separate remedies and can both be applied for the same infringement.

queries.query: How do Articles 9 and 10 distinguish two categories of sensitive data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 9 covers special categories including health, biometric, genetic, racial data; Article 10 covers criminal conviction and offence data; both require heightened protection but Article 10 data can only be processed under official authority.

queries.query: How do Articles 7 and 8 modify consent requirements for different age groups?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 7 sets general conditions for consent; Article 8 provides specific conditions for children below 16 requiring parental consent; Article 8 is a lex specialis modifying Article 7 for children.

queries.query: How do Articles 37 and 39 define the DPO's appointment and function?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 37 defines when and how a DPO must be appointed; Article 39 defines the tasks the DPO must perform; together they create the complete DPO framework from appointment to function.

queries.query: How do Articles 38 and 39 protect the DPO's independence and define tasks?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 38 ensures the DPO's independence by requiring reporting to the highest management and protecting against dismissal; Article 39 defines specific tasks including monitoring compliance; independence is a prerequisite for effective task performance.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 17 interact regarding storage limitation and erasure?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5(1)(e) requires that data not be kept longer than necessary; Article 17 provides the data subject with a right to erasure; the storage limitation principle requires proactive deletion while the erasure right is a reactive right.

queries.query: How do Articles 12 and 15 together enable meaningful exercise of data subject rights?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 12 sets the manner of communication for exercising rights; Article 15 defines the substantive right of access; effective exercise of the access right requires the procedural rules of Article 12 to be followed.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 89 allow research to override some data protection principles?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6 requires a lawful basis for processing; Article 89 allows derogations from certain rights for research purposes; the research exception permits wider use of data than would otherwise be lawful.

queries.query: How do Articles 24 and 25 define proactive data protection obligations?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 24 requires implementing appropriate measures to ensure compliance; Article 25 requires data protection by design and by default; together they impose a duty to build privacy into systems rather than add it afterwards.

queries.query: How do Articles 45 and 49 form the hierarchy for third country transfers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 45 adequacy decisions are the primary mechanism for third country transfers; Article 49 derogations are available only where there is no adequacy decision and no appropriate safeguards; they operate in a hierarchical order.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 88 interact in the employment context?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6 provides lawful bases for processing; Article 88 allows Member States to provide more specific rules for employment processing; the employment context may require a combination of consent and legal obligation.

queries.query: How do Articles 21 and 18 provide overlapping data subject protections?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 21 provides the right to object to processing; Article 18 provides the right to restriction when processing is under challenge; when an objection is made the processing must be restricted pending the controller's response.

queries.query: How do Articles 4 and 3 together define the geographical scope of GDPR?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 4 defines 'establishment' and 'main establishment'; Article 3 specifies the territorial scope; the definition of establishment in Article 4 determines which entities fall within the territorial scope.

queries.query: How do Articles 80 and 82 together enable collective redress?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 80 enables representative actions by not-for-profit organisations; Article 82 provides for compensation for damage; together they enable organisations to seek compensation on behalf of data subjects.

queries.query: How do Articles 57 and 58 define the tasks and powers of supervisory authorities?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 57 lists tasks including investigation and advice; Article 58 provides specific powers to carry out those tasks; tasks describe what authorities must do and powers describe what they can do to achieve it.

queries.query: How do Articles 2 and 9 interact for special category data processing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 2 defines the material scope of GDPR; Article 9 adds an additional layer of protection for special categories; within the scope of GDPR, processing of special categories is subject to additional conditions.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 89 interact regarding purpose limitation for research?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5 requires purpose limitation; Article 89 allows further processing for archiving, scientific research, statistics, or historical research as compatible purposes subject to safeguards.

queries.query: How do Articles 15 and 22 together address transparency in automated decisions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 15 gives the right to access including information about logic of automated decisions; Article 22 gives the right not to be subject to purely automated decisions; both address the transparency and fairness of automated processing.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 23 interact regarding lawful bases and restrictions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6 provides lawful bases for processing; Article 23 allows Member States to restrict certain obligations when national interests are at stake; restrictions under Article 23 must respect the substance of the rights.

queries.query: How do Articles 28 and 29 define the relationship between controller and processor?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 28 establishes the legal framework for processor relationships; Article 29 requires that processors act only on instructions; both define a relationship where the processor is subordinate to the controller.

queries.query: How do Articles 31 and 58 work together in supervisory cooperation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 31 requires controllers to cooperate with supervisory authorities; Article 58 gives supervisory authorities investigative and corrective powers to enforce that cooperation; cooperation is both obligatory and enforceable.

queries.query: How do Articles 12 and 23 balance transparency and restrictions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 12 requires transparent communication to data subjects; Article 23 allows restrictions on this transparency for specified public interest reasons; restrictions must be necessary and proportionate.

queries.query: How do Articles 82 and 84 provide complementary enforcement mechanisms?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 82 provides for civil compensation to individuals for damage caused; Article 84 requires Member States to provide for additional penalties; both are enforcement tools separate from administrative fines under Article 83.

queries.query: How do Articles 20 and 17 interact in portability and erasure?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Both Article 20 and Article 17 deal with the situation when a data subject wants to leave a controller; Article 20 enables them to take their data away; Article 17 enables them to have it deleted; both facilitate exit.

queries.query: How do Articles 37 and 38 together define the DPO's position in the organisation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 37 requires designation of a DPO with expert knowledge; Article 38 requires the DPO to be involved in all relevant matters and to have necessary resources; together they ensure the DPO has both expertise and access.

queries.query: How do Articles 61 and 62 enable cross-border supervisory cooperation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 61 provides for mutual assistance between supervisory authorities; Article 62 provides for joint operations; both enable supervisory authorities to act together for consistent application of GDPR across borders.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 9 require different levels of justification?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6 requires at least one lawful basis from a list of six; Article 9 requires both a lawful basis under Article 6 and one of the additional conditions in Article 9(2); processing special categories requires double justification.

queries.query: How do Articles 14 and 23 interact regarding information obligations and restrictions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 14 requires providing information when data is obtained from other sources; Article 23 allows restrictions on this obligation for national security or other interests; the restriction must be provided for in law.

queries.query: How do Articles 77 and 80 together enable different complaint mechanisms?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 77 allows individual data subjects to file complaints; Article 80 allows not-for-profit organisations to file on behalf of data subjects; together they provide both individual and collective enforcement mechanisms.

queries.query: How do Articles 46 and 49 create a hierarchy for transfers without adequacy decisions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 46 provides appropriate safeguards for transfers where no adequacy decision exists; Article 49 provides derogations only where neither adequacy decisions nor safeguards are available; Article 49 is a last resort.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 25 reinforce each other in data minimisation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5(1)(c) requires data minimisation as a principle; Article 25 requires it to be implemented by design and by default; the principle is supported by the technical and organisational obligation to implement it in practice.

queries.query: How do Articles 13 and 22 together ensure transparency in automated processing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 13 requires providing information about automated decision-making at the time of data collection; Article 22 provides the substantive right regarding automated decisions; Article 13 provides advance notice of what Article 22 governs.

queries.query: How do Articles 83 and 28 interact when a processor causes a data breach?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 28 requires the processor to notify the controller immediately of a breach; Article 83 can impose fines on processors who fail to comply with their obligations; processors can be held independently liable.

queries.query: How do Articles 4 and 11 interact regarding anonymised data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 4 defines personal data as data relating to an identifiable natural person; Article 11 deals with processing that does not require identification; truly anonymised data falls outside GDPR while pseudonymised data remains within it.

queries.query: How do Articles 58 and 65 interact when supervisory authorities disagree?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 58 gives each supervisory authority enforcement powers; Article 65 provides for binding decisions by the Board when authorities disagree; the Board's decision overrides the national authority.

queries.query: How do Articles 30 and 31 together define the documentation and cooperation obligations?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 30 requires maintaining records of processing activities as internal documentation; Article 31 requires cooperation with the supervisory authority to provide that documentation on request; records enable cooperation.

queries.query: How do Articles 79 and 84 provide judicial and non-judicial remedies?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 79 provides for effective judicial remedy in national courts; Article 84 requires Member States to lay down non-judicial penalties; together they provide both judicial and administrative enforcement at national level.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 13 interact in informing data subjects of the legal basis?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6 requires a lawful basis for processing; Article 13(1)(c) requires the controller to inform the data subject of the legal basis and legitimate interests; the data subject must be told the justification for processing.

queries.query: How do Articles 25 and 32 complement each other in security?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 25 requires privacy by design and by default to be implemented; Article 32 requires appropriate technical and organisational security measures; both address the technical implementation of GDPR but from different angles.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 6 together establish the fundamental processing framework?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5 sets out the principles that apply to all processing; Article 6 provides the lawful bases that must underpin processing; both must be satisfied for any processing of personal data to be lawful.

queries.query: How do Articles 4 and 35 interact regarding the definition of high risk?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 4 defines personal data and processing; Article 35 requires a DPIA for processing that is likely to result in high risk to rights and freedoms; the definition of processing in Article 4 determines when Article 35 applies.

queries.query: How do Articles 22 and 9 interact for automated decisions involving special category data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 22(1) restricts solely automated decisions; Article 22(4) explicitly prohibits basing such decisions on special category data except with explicit consent or substantial public interest; Articles 9 and 22 provide layered protection.

queries.query: How do Articles 58 and 83 together define the supervisory authority's enforcement toolkit?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 58 provides the full range of corrective powers including warnings, reprimands, orders, and bans; Article 83 adds administrative fines as the most significant financial penalty; together they give supervisory authorities a comprehensive toolkit.

queries.query: How do Articles 34 and 12 interact in communicating breaches?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 34 requires communication of data breaches to data subjects when there is high risk; Article 12 sets the manner of communication which must be clear and transparent; breach notifications must comply with both provisions.

queries.query: How do Articles 18 and 21 provide complementary protection during disputes?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 21 provides the right to object to processing; Article 18 provides the right to restriction pending resolution of the objection; restriction operates as an interim measure while the objection is being considered.

queries.query: How do Articles 4 and 6 interact regarding identifiability and lawful basis?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 4 defines personal data as information relating to an identifiable person; Article 6 requires a lawful basis; if a person cannot be identified the data is anonymous and falls outside both provisions.

queries.query: How do Articles 9 and 88 interact for sensitive data in employment?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 9 restricts processing of special categories; Article 88 allows Member States to provide specific rules for employment; employment may create a basis for processing special category data subject to safeguards.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 83 together establish the consequences of principle violations?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5 establishes the fundamental principles; Article 83(5)(a) provides that violations of the basic principles are subject to the highest fine tier; violating the principles is the most serious category of GDPR infringement.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 5 interact in the principle of lawfulness?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5(1)(a) requires processing to be lawful; Article 6 defines what makes processing lawful by specifying the legal bases; Article 5 sets the standard and Article 6 provides the mechanism for meeting it.

queries.query: How do Articles 12 and 17 together enable effective exercise of the erasure right?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 17 gives the substantive right to erasure; Article 12 requires the controller to respond within one month and provides for extension; without the procedural framework of Article 12 the substantive right in Article 17 would be ineffective.

queries.query: What is the right of employees regarding monitoring at the workplace?
queries.ground_truth_answer: GDPR allows Member States to provide rules for processing in the employment context including monitoring; any monitoring must be proportionate, transparent, and have a legitimate basis.

queries.query: What is the role of the supervisory authority as the lead authority?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The lead supervisory authority is the sole interlocutor for cross-border processing; it coordinates with other concerned authorities; it issues the final decision binding on all.

queries.query: What is the right to obtain human review of a solely automated decision?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The data subject has the right to obtain human intervention, to express their point of view, and to contest the decision; the controller must implement suitable measures.

queries.query: What are the provisions relating to international transfers to organisations?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Personal data may be transferred to international organisations on the basis of standard contractual clauses or where adequacy of protection is assessed; the Commission may adopt implementing acts.

queries.query: What obligations does a processor have if it processes data outside instructions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: If the processor processes data outside the scope of the controller's instructions it becomes a controller with respect to that processing and is subject to the same obligations.

queries.query: What are the conditions for processing under Article 6(1)(e) for public tasks?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Processing must be necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in exercise of official authority vested in the controller; the basis must be provided in Union or Member State law.

queries.query: What is the right to obtain information about international transfers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The data subject has the right to know of any transfer to a third country or international organisation and the safeguards that apply; this information must be provided as part of the right of access.

queries.query: What are the provisions regarding data protection seals and marks?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Certifications, seals and marks shall be issued for a maximum period of three years and may be renewed; the Commission may provide further requirements for certification mechanisms.

queries.query: What are the conditions for derogations from rights for historical research?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Derogations from the rights of access, rectification, restriction, and objection may be provided for historical research under safeguards including pseudonymisation and minimisation.

queries.query: What is the definition of an enterprise under GDPR?
queries.ground_truth_answer: An enterprise means a natural or legal person engaged in an economic activity, irrespective of its legal form, including partnerships or associations regularly engaged in an economic activity.

queries.query: What are the provisions on processing relating to public health?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Processing of health data for reasons of public interest in the area of public health including protection against serious cross-border threats to health is permitted under Article 9(2)(i).

queries.query: What is the right to know about the retention period for personal data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The data subject has the right to know the period for which data will be stored or the criteria used to determine that period; this information must be provided at the time of collection.

queries.query: What are the conditions for processing data for electoral purposes?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Processing data revealing political opinions for electoral activities is subject to Member State law derogations; appropriate safeguards must be in place and the processing must be necessary.

queries.query: What are the supervisory authority's authorisation powers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Authorisation powers include approving binding corporate rules, certifying processors, approving standard contractual clauses, and authorising specific transfer mechanisms.

queries.query: What are the obligations of supervisory authorities to publish guidelines?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Supervisory authorities shall provide guidance and recommendations on data protection issues; they shall promote public awareness; they shall inform data subjects of their rights.

queries.query: What are the requirements for GDPR compliance for small businesses?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Small businesses with fewer than 250 employees are exempt from the record-keeping obligation unless processing poses a risk, is carried out regularly, or involves special categories.

queries.query: What is the scope of the right to portability regarding data provided to services?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The right applies to data the data subject has actively and knowingly provided; it also covers data generated through their activity such as browsing history or health data from a wearable device.

queries.query: What are the provisions regarding mandatory data minimisation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Data minimisation requires that only data necessary for the stated purpose is collected; by default only necessary data should be processed and settings must not allow more than what is needed.

queries.query: What are the criteria for determining whether processing poses high risk?
queries.ground_truth_answer: High risk is indicated by evaluation of personal aspects, processing of special categories on a large scale, systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas, and use of new technological solutions.

queries.query: What is the duty of the DPO to maintain secrecy?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The DPO shall be bound by secrecy or confidentiality concerning the performance of their tasks in accordance with Union or Member State law; this duty continues after the DPO's term.

queries.query: What is the obligation to respond to supervisory authority requests?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The controller and processor and their representatives shall cooperate with the supervisory authority on request in the performance of its tasks; this obligation is unconditional.

queries.query: What are the specific protections for processing of employees' data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Processing must be subject to specific rules ensuring dignity and fundamental rights; monitoring of performance is subject to proportionality; health data in employment requires specific justification.

queries.query: What is the right to clear and plain language in data protection policies?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The controller must communicate with data subjects in clear and plain language; information must be concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible; it must use child-friendly language when directed at children.

queries.query: What are the provisions on joint and several liability of controller and processor?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where both a controller and a processor are responsible for the damage the controller and processor shall be held jointly and severally liable; each may seek contribution from the other.

queries.query: What are the provisions for reporting on GDPR activities by supervisory authorities?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Each supervisory authority shall prepare an annual report; it must be submitted to national parliament and government; the Board shall publish a combined report.

queries.query: What is the obligation to implement pseudonymisation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Pseudonymisation is mentioned as an appropriate technical measure for security; it is not mandatory but is recommended as a safeguard; it reduces risk but the data remains personal data.

queries.query: What are the provisions for protecting minors' data in online services?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Online service providers must take reasonable steps to verify parental consent; Member States may lower the age threshold; age verification cannot require excessive data collection.

queries.query: What are the data protection obligations for political parties?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Processing of data revealing political opinions requires explicit consent or another Article 9(2) condition; political parties must comply with GDPR when processing member and voter data.

queries.query: What are the provisions for accessing public sector data for research?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Public sector data may be made available for research purposes subject to appropriate safeguards; GDPR must be reconciled with the right of public access to documents.

queries.query: What are the specific obligations of certification bodies?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Certification bodies must be accredited; they must assess before issuing certificates; they must monitor compliance; they must revoke certificates when requirements are not met.

queries.query: What are the provisions for the right to complain before the Member State courts?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Data subjects may bring proceedings before courts in the Member State of their habitual residence; where the controller is a public authority the courts of that State shall have jurisdiction.

queries.query: What are the provisions for obtaining mandatory prior consultation with supervisory authority?

queries.query: What are the obligations of joint controllers to inform data subjects?

queries.query: What are the principles for assessing adequacy of a third country?

queries.query: What are the GDPR obligations when outsourcing data processing to a third party?

queries.query: What conditions apply to lawful processing for pension fund administration?

queries.query: What conditions apply to data protection when using biometric access systems?

queries.query: What conditions apply to the right to data portability for financial services?

queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 13 requires providing information about purposes and legal basis; Article 7 requires that consent be informed; together they ensure that when consent is the basis the data subject has full information to make an informed decision.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 25 interact in implementing data minimisation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6 requires a lawful basis; Article 25 requires that by default only the minimum data necessary is collected; the lawful basis cannot justify collection of more data than what is minimally necessary.

queries.query: How do Articles 51 and 52 together ensure independent supervisory authority?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 51 requires each Member State to establish an independent supervisory authority; Article 52 guarantees the independence of the authority and its members; both provisions work together to ensure genuine independence.

queries.query: How do Articles 83 and 5 interact when the accountability principle is violated?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5(2) establishes the accountability principle; Article 83(5)(a) provides that violations of the basic principles including accountability are subject to the highest tier of administrative fines; accountability violations are the most severely punished.

queries.query: How do Articles 46 and 40 together provide an approved code of conduct transfer mechanism?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 40 provides for development and approval of codes of conduct; Article 46(2)(e) allows adherence to an approved code to be an appropriate safeguard for international transfers; the code must address the specific protections needed for third country transfers.

queries.query: How do Articles 35 and 32 together govern high-risk processing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 35 requires a DPIA for high-risk processing before it begins; Article 32 requires security measures appropriate to the risk; the DPIA assesses the risk and informs what security measures under Article 32 are required.

queries.query: How do Articles 79 and 77 enable simultaneous remedies?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 77 provides for administrative complaints to supervisory authorities; Article 79 provides for judicial proceedings against controllers; both can be pursued simultaneously; supervisory authority action does not bar judicial remedy.

queries.query: How do Articles 4 and 17 define the scope of the right to erasure?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 4 defines personal data broadly; Article 17 grants the right to erasure of personal data; the broad definition in Article 4 determines the scope of data that must be erased under Article 17.

queries.query: How do Articles 88 and 9 together protect employees' health data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 9 restricts processing of health data; Article 88 allows Member States to provide specific rules for employment; in the employment context specific national rules may provide for health data processing subject to appropriate safeguards.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 14 interact when data is obtained without the data subject's knowledge?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6 requires a lawful basis even when data is obtained from third parties; Article 14 requires the data subject to be informed within a reasonable period; both apply when data is collected without the data subject's direct involvement.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 83 work together as the basis for the highest tier of fines?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5 establishes the fundamental principles; Article 83(5)(a) imposes the highest fines for violations of those principles; the more fundamental the principle violated the more severe the sanction.

queries.query: How do Articles 36 and 58 interact in the prior consultation process?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 36 requires prior consultation with the supervisory authority for high-risk processing; Article 58 gives the supervisory authority the power to provide written advice; the consultation triggers the advisory power.

queries.query: How do Articles 15 and 20 compare in the content of access and portability?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 15 gives access to a copy of personal data; Article 20 gives the right to receive data in a machine-readable format; access is broader but portability is in a more useful technical format; both rights can be exercised simultaneously.

queries.query: How do Articles 4 and 83 interact in the scope of fines for each entity?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 4 defines controllers, processors, and enterprises; Article 83 bases fines on the worldwide annual turnover of the undertaking; the definition of undertaking determines the fines base.

queries.query: How do Articles 13 and 22 together address transparency in profiling?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 13 requires informing data subjects about profiling activities at the time of data collection; Article 22 provides rights regarding solely automated decisions including profiling; together they ensure both advance notice and ongoing protection.

queries.query: How do Articles 9 and 35 interact for special category data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 9 restricts processing of special categories; Article 35(3)(b) specifically requires a DPIA for large-scale processing of special categories; the special nature of the data automatically triggers the DPIA requirement.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 25 together operationalise privacy as a design principle?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5 sets the principles including data minimisation and purpose limitation; Article 25 requires those principles to be implemented technically by design and by default; Article 5 defines the goal and Article 25 defines how to achieve it technically.

queries.query: How do Articles 4 and 28 define the controller-processor distinction?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 4 defines a controller as one who determines purposes and means and a processor as one who processes on behalf; Article 28 governs the relationship; the distinction in Article 4 determines whether Article 28 applies.

queries.query: How do Articles 51 and 68 relate in national and European data protection oversight?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 51 requires each Member State to establish an independent national supervisory authority; Article 68 creates the European Data Protection Board at EU level; the national authorities form the Board.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 21 interact for scientific and public interest processing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6(1)(e) permits processing for public tasks; Article 21(6) restricts the right to object for scientific research when it would render the research impossible; together they define the limited right to object to public interest research.

queries.query: How do Articles 83 and 28 interact when a processor independently processes data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 28 requires processors to process only on instructions; Article 83 provides that processors are independently liable for fines; a processor who processes outside instructions may face direct enforcement action.

queries.query: How do Articles 9 and 22 provide layered protection for health data automated decisions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Health data is a special category under Article 9; Article 22(4) prohibits basing solely automated decisions on special category data unless explicit consent is obtained or substantial public interest applies; both provisions must be satisfied.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 32 together implement the integrity and confidentiality principle?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5(1)(f) establishes integrity and confidentiality as a principle; Article 32 operationalises this principle by requiring technical and organisational security measures; the principle in Article 5 is implemented through the obligation in Article 32.

queries.query: How do Articles 3 and 27 together require non-EU controllers to comply with GDPR?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 3 gives GDPR extra-territorial application to non-EU controllers targeting EU residents; Article 27 requires such controllers to designate a representative in the EU; together they ensure that EU residents can enforce their rights against foreign controllers.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 9 interact when special category data is processed for a contract?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6(1)(b) permits processing for contract performance; Article 9 requires an additional condition for special category data in the contract; both must be satisfied; a contract basis alone is insufficient for special categories.

queries.query: How do Articles 44 and 46 form the framework for transfers without adequacy decisions?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 44 establishes the principle that transfers must comply with Chapter V; where no adequacy decision exists Article 46 provides for transfers subject to appropriate safeguards; the two articles establish the primary transfer mechanism hierarchy.

queries.query: How do Articles 12 and 11 interact when the controller cannot identify the data subject?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 11 provides that controllers are not required to maintain information solely to identify data subjects for the purpose of exercising rights; Article 12 requires the controller to inform the data subject that identification is not possible.

queries.query: How do Articles 17 and 89 interact when erasure is requested for historical research data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 17 provides the right to erasure; Article 89 permits derogations from the erasure right for historical research where erasure would seriously impair the research; Member State law must provide for this derogation.

queries.query: How do Articles 20 and 7 interact in data portability and withdrawal of consent?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 7 permits withdrawal of consent at any time; Article 20 gives the right to receive data in a portable format; together they enable a data subject to withdraw consent and take their data to a competitor.

queries.query: How do Articles 64 and 65 define the Board's opinion and binding decision powers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 64 provides for consistency opinions by the Board on certain matters; Article 65 provides for binding decisions in disputed cases; opinions are advisory but binding decisions are enforceable.

queries.query: How do Articles 82 and 83 together provide comprehensive enforcement?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 82 provides for civil liability for individuals suffering damage; Article 83 provides for administrative fines by supervisory authorities; both can be applied for the same infringement; civil and regulatory enforcement are complementary.

queries.query: How do Articles 28 and 26 differ when two organisations share responsibilities?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 28 applies where one organisation processes data on behalf of another following instructions; Article 26 applies where two organisations jointly determine purposes and means; the key question is who controls the processing.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 17 interact when processing is based on legal obligation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Where Article 6(1)(c) legal obligation is the basis the controller must comply with the law which may require retention; Article 17(3)(b) exempts erasure where the processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation; the obligation prevails over the erasure right.

queries.query: How do Articles 47 and 56 interact in binding corporate rules and lead authority?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 47 requires BCRs to be approved by the competent supervisory authority; Article 56 designates the lead supervisory authority for cross-border processing; the lead authority typically approves BCRs for multinational groups.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 13 together ensure the transparency principle?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5(1)(a) requires transparency as a fundamental processing principle; Article 13 implements that principle by specifying what information must be provided; the principle in Article 5 is given concrete content by Article 13.

queries.query: How do Articles 31 and 82 interact in the obligation to cooperate?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 31 requires controllers to cooperate with supervisory authorities; a controller who obstructs an investigation may face a fine under Article 83(4); failure to cooperate may also reduce the possibility of mitigating a fine.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 21 interact when processing is for a public task?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6(1)(e) permits processing for public tasks; Article 21 gives a right to object on grounds relating to particular situation; the objection may be overridden if the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds as part of the public task.

queries.query: How do Articles 4 and 89 interact in defining what constitutes scientific research?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 4 does not define scientific research; Recital 159 clarifies that it covers both publicly and privately funded research; Article 89 provides safeguards; together they establish that the research must be genuine and subject to appropriate oversight.

queries.query: How do Articles 13 and 14 interact with the principle of fairness?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Articles 13 and 14 require proactive provision of information; the principle of fairness in Article 5(1)(a) requires that data subjects are not misled about how their data is used; both articles implement the fairness principle.

queries.query: How do Articles 37 and 83 interact when a required DPO is not appointed?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 37 requires appointment of a DPO in specified circumstances; failure to appoint is an infringement of controller obligations under Article 83(4); the fine can be up to 10 million euros or 2% of global turnover.

queries.query: How do Articles 9 and 83 interact for breaches involving special category data?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Breaches relating to special category data under Article 9 may attract fines under Article 83(5) as violations of basic conditions for processing; the special category nature of the data may be an aggravating factor in determining the fine.

queries.query: How do Articles 46 and 47 compare for group and non-group transfers?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 46 provides various safeguards for transfers to third countries; Article 47 specifically addresses intra-group transfers through BCRs; BCRs under Article 47 are a specialised form of the safeguards in Article 46.

queries.query: How do Articles 13 and 37 interact in informing data subjects about the DPO?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 13(1)(b) requires the controller to provide the contact details of the DPO where applicable; Article 37 requires a DPO to be designated in certain cases; where a DPO exists their contact details must be provided to data subjects.

queries.query: How do Articles 6 and 5 interact in ensuring lawfulness of processing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5(1)(a) requires lawfulness as a processing principle; Article 6 defines what constitutes lawful processing; satisfying Article 6 is a necessary but not sufficient condition for lawfulness; all Article 5 principles must also be met.

queries.query: How do Articles 51 and 77 together enable enforcement of data subject rights?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 51 requires each Member State to establish an independent supervisory authority; Article 77 gives data subjects the right to complain to that authority; the supervisory authority created by Article 51 is the body that receives complaints under Article 77.

queries.query: How do Articles 32 and 33 form a risk management cycle?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 32 requires risk-appropriate security measures before and during processing; Article 33 requires notification when those measures fail and a breach occurs; together they create a cycle of prevention and response.

queries.query: How do Articles 21 and 17 compare when the right to object and right to erasure are both exercised?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The right to object and the right to erasure may both be exercised for the same processing; Article 21 requires stopping the processing; Article 17 requires erasing the data; stopping processing alone may be insufficient if retention is not justified.

queries.query: How do Articles 24 and 5 together define the accountability obligation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 5(2) establishes accountability as a principle requiring the controller to demonstrate compliance; Article 24 requires the controller to implement measures and be able to demonstrate their effectiveness; both are about proof of compliance not just compliance.

queries.query: How do Articles 28 and 32 define the shared security obligation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 28 requires the controller to use only processors with sufficient security guarantees; Article 32 imposes security obligations on both controllers and processors directly; together they create a shared but differentiated responsibility.

queries.query: How do Articles 83 and 58 interact when a supervisory authority imposes a fine?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 58(2)(i) specifically empowers supervisory authorities to impose fines; Article 83 defines the conditions, criteria, and limits; Article 58 is the source of the power and Article 83 is the framework for how it must be exercised.

queries.query: How do Articles 5 and 6 together establish the minimum conditions for lawful processing?
queries.ground_truth_answer: Article 6 requires a lawful basis; Article 5 requires all six processing principles to be met; having a lawful basis under Article 6 is necessary but processing must also be fair, transparent, purposeful, minimal, accurate, and secure under Article 5.
